\hypertarget{doc-rbac-model}{%
\chapter{The Akeyless authorization model}\label{doc-rbac-model}}

Verified against docs.akeyless.io (RBAC, Sub-Claims, CLI reference), the Akeyless OpenAPI and the
Terraform provider v2.0.5. Items marked \textbf{VERIFY} are not confirmed by a primary source.

\hypertarget{objects-and-namespaces}{%
\section{Objects and namespaces}\label{objects-and-namespaces}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Items} (static/rotated/dynamic secrets, keys, certificates, PKI/SSH issuers), \textbf{Targets},
  \textbf{Access Roles} and \textbf{Auth Methods} live in separate trees, each named by a slash path.
\item
  Item folders are implicit: creating \texttt{/a/b/c} creates \texttt{/a} and \texttt{/a/b}. \texttt{folder\ create} /
  \texttt{akeyless\_folder} only adds empty folders, description, tags and delete protection.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{identity}{%
\section{Identity}\label{identity}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A caller authenticates through an \textbf{Auth Method} (API key, OIDC, SAML, LDAP, OAuth2/JWT, AWS IAM,
  Azure AD, GCP, K8s, certificate, Universal Identity, ...). The token carries the claims of that login.
\item
  There are \textbf{no RBAC user or group objects}. Human scoping comes from IdP claims (e.g. \texttt{groups}).
\item
  Akeyless \textbf{Groups} (\texttt{create-group}, \texttt{akeyless\_group}) bundle auth methods for Akeyless
  \textbf{OIDC applications} - they are not RBAC groups.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{access-roles}{%
\section{Access Roles}\label{access-roles}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Default deny}: no association, no access. The built-in admin role has full access.
\item
  A role = \textbf{rules} + \textbf{management-plane settings}; a role is bound to auth methods by
  \textbf{associations} that may carry \textbf{sub-claims}.
\end{itemize}

\texttt{item-rule} (default) & items & \texttt{read,\ list,\ create,\ update,\ delete,\ deny} \\
\texttt{target-rule} & targets & same \\
\texttt{role-rule} & access roles & same \\
\texttt{auth-method-rule} & auth methods & same \\
\texttt{sra-rule} & Secure Remote Access & \texttt{allow\_access,\ request\_access,\ justify\_access\_only,\ approval\_authority,\ upload\_files,\ download\_files} \\
\texttt{ara-rule} & Agentic Runtime Authority & \texttt{allow\_access} (API/CLI; not documented by provider 2.0.5 - VERIFY) \\
\end{longtable}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Every capability implies \texttt{list}.
\item
  \texttt{deny} overrides all other permissions on the matched path (docs). Prove cross-role behaviour
  with Impersonate As / \texttt{akl\_verify.py}. \texttt{deny} does \textbf{not} apply to SRA paths.
\item
  \texttt{approval\_authority} cannot be combined with \texttt{request\_access}.
\item
  Wildcards: \texttt{*} at the end (\texttt{/payments/*}) or as a prefix (\texttt{/payments/devops-*}); \texttt{+} = any
  characters within exactly one segment (\texttt{/payments/+/prod/*}).
\item
  Templated paths from sub-claims, e.g. \texttt{/\{\{groups\}\}/\{\{email\}\}/*} (the docs show both \texttt{\{\{x\}\}} and
  \texttt{\{x\}} - VERIFY on your account).
\item
  Temporary rules: \texttt{set-role-rule\ -\/-ttl\ \textless{}minutes\textgreater{}} (CLI/API only).
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{sub-claims-on-associations}{%
\subsection{Sub-claims (on associations)}\label{sub-claims-on-associations}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Within one key, comma-separated values = OR; different keys = AND.
\item
  Values accept \texttt{*} and \texttt{?} globs.
\item
  Keys and values are case-sensitive unless the association sets \texttt{case\_sensitive=false}.
\item
  Gateway \textgreater= 4.19 accepts explicit \texttt{AND} / \texttt{OR} inside one key\textquotesingle s value, evaluated left to right.
\item
  \texttt{force\_sub\_claims=true} on an auth method makes every association to it require sub-claims.
\item
  \texttt{akeyless\ describe-sub-claims} prints the claims of the current token.
\end{itemize}

\texttt{audit\_access} & none, own, scoped, all \\

\texttt{gw\_analytics\_access}, \texttt{sra\_reports\_access}, \texttt{event\_center\_access}, \texttt{isi\_access}, \texttt{unlock\_secrets}, \texttt{approve\_access\_request} & none, scoped, all \\

"scoped" = objects the caller can list. Internally these are stored as special rules
(\texttt{search-rule}, \texttt{reports-rule}, ... with paths \texttt{/*}, \texttt{/self}, \texttt{/scoped}).

\hypertarget{anti-escalation}{%
\section{Anti-escalation}\label{anti-escalation}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A non-admin can only create or change roles that grant capabilities they themselves hold on the path.
\item
  A non-admin creator\textquotesingle s own \texttt{deny} rules are copied onto roles they create. Terraform exposes them
  as read-only \texttt{restricted\_rules} and never removes them.
\item
  Consequence: the identity that applies RBAC must hold everything it grants (admin-equivalent).
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{gateway-access---the-second-layer}{%
\section{Gateway access - the second layer}\label{gateway-access---the-second-layer}}

RBAC decides which \textbf{objects} a caller can touch. \textbf{Gateway Allowed Access} decides who may
administer a given Gateway and which features (\texttt{defaults,\ targets,\ classic\_keys,\ automatic\_migration,\ ldap\_auth,\ dynamic\_secret,\ k8s\_auth,\ log\_forwarding,\ zero\_knowledge\_encryption,\ rotated\_secret,\ caching,\ event\_forwarding,\ admin,\ kmip,\ general,\ rotate\_secret\_value}). Creating rotated/dynamic secrets on a Gateway requires both layers.

\hypertarget{inspection}{%
\section{Inspection}\label{inspection}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{akeyless\ describe-permissions\ -\/-path\ P\ -\/-type\ item\textbar{}am\textbar{}role\textbar{}target} - the \textbf{caller\textquotesingle s own}
  permissions on P (\texttt{client\_permissions}).
\item
  \texttt{akeyless\ reverse-rbac\ -\/-path\ P\ -\/-type\ item\textbar{}am\textbar{}role\textbar{}target\textbar{}sra\textbar{}ara} - which auth methods/roles
  reach P.
\item
  Console: account menu -\textgreater{} \textbf{Impersonate As} (auth method + sub-claims).
\end{itemize}
